description: Knowledge base extracted from Renad Eid Product Design Roadmaps

sections.title_ar: Renad Eid · خرائط طريق التصميم والإنتاج 2026
sections.content: Complete design and production roadmaps for product designers and teams. Covers workflow from brief to handoff, UI/UX principles, e-commerce vs SaaS models, idea to production pipeline, and standard operating procedures.

sections.title_ar: Roadmap عملي من استلام الـ Brief إلى الـ Handoff
sections.content: 12-step design workflow: Discovery, Problem Framing, Idea Generation, Prioritization, User Flows, Wireframing, UI Direction, Microcopy, Prototyping, Testing, Handoff, and Review. Includes AI tool usage at each step (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini) and best practices for Figma, Maze, and Claude.

sections.title_ar: Roadmap مبني على مبادئ UI / UX
sections.content: 8 core UI/UX principles applied systematically: Hierarchy, Clarity, User Control, Consistency, Error Prevention, Visibility, Recognition over Recall. Includes 3 principle cards and case study showing 67% to 38% improvement in cart abandonment through checkout redesign.

sections.title_ar: أمثلة على E-commerce و SaaS Models
sections.content: Comparison framework for E-commerce vs SaaS products. E-commerce focuses on trust, conversion, speed, discovery (PLP→PDP→Cart→Checkout). SaaS focuses on onboarding, retention, workflows, permissions (Dashboard→Settings→Teams). Case study: Bazaar dual interface (marketplace + seller dashboard).

12-phase end-to-end roadmap: Intake, Scope, Spec, IA/UX, AI Model Test, Code Planning, Coding, Source Control, Backend, Frontend Preview, QA, Release. Tool stack includes Perplexity, Claude, Figma, Claude Code, GitHub, Supabase, Vercel. Complementary tools: Linear, Maze, Loom, Sentry, PostHog, Cursor.
12-step standard operating procedure checklist for every project. Sequential workflow from brief through production with clear accountability and deliverables at each stage.
Audience-specific guidance for Junior Designers, Product Teams, and Engineering teams. Key reminders for successful project delivery and collaboration.

sections.title_en: A practical guide to AI Mastery
sections.content: Comprehensive AI guide covering landscape of tools, practical workflows, decision-making frameworks, core concepts, product architectures, and learning paths for product designers and teams.

6 AI tool categories: 1) Conversation & Reasoning (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini), 2) Search with Sources (Perplexity, Gemini), 3) Coding Agents & IDEs (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Antigravity), 4) Studios & Experimentation (Google AI Studio, Vercel v0), 5) Building & Deployment (Vercel, Supabase, Firebase), 6) Image & Visual Design (Nano Banana Pro, Midjourney, Adobe Firefly). Includes 18-row comparison table.

6 workflow applications: Research & Understanding, Writing & Documentation, Coding, Design, Data, Communications. Guardrails: No secrets, verify output, keep human judgment. Practical examples for each workflow category.

Decision tree for AI tool selection based on task type: Updated facts → Perplexity; Code execution → Claude Code; Images → Image tools; Deep thinking → Claude; API testing → Google AI Studio. Visual flowchart for quick reference.

8 foundational AI concepts: LLM (predicts next token), Models (sizes/speeds/costs), Agents (plans/executes/monitors in loop), Skills (reusable capabilities), MCP (Model Context Protocol), Tokens (pricing/context units), Memory (persistent recall), Context (temporary visibility). Visual flowchart included.

6 scaffold components around AI models: System Prompt, Tools, Memory & Context, Loop (execution cycle), Retrieval (RAG), Guards & Evals. 4-step improvement methodology: Measure with evals → Improve context → Add tools → Iterate prompt.

6 AI product architectures (escalating complexity): 1) Wrapper (prompt + interface), 2) RAG App (model + knowledge base), 3) Agentic (agents with tools), 4) Multi-Agent (specialized agents + coordination), 5) Copilot Embedded (AI inside existing product), 6) Fine-tuned (model trained on own data). Each includes examples, metrics, and case studies.
Visual mind map of AI concepts and relationships for quick reference and understanding of the AI ecosystem.
Deep dive into Claude Code and Codex for AI-assisted development. Best practices, workflows, and mastery techniques.
Using CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md files for persistent context and agent configuration. Best practices for structuring context files.
Setting up and managing AI agent environments. Agent orchestration, tools, and best practices.
Building automated workflows and processes using AI. Integration patterns and automation strategies.
Building AI models from scratch. Training, fine-tuning, and deployment strategies.
Structured learning path for AI mastery. Resources, milestones, and progression strategy.
Comprehensive UI/UX design guide covering foundations, processes, research, information architecture, visual principles, design systems, accessibility, and career roadmap.
UX vs UI distinction. UX = Experience (did user reach goal easily?). UI = Interface (is it clear and beautiful?). TV remote analogy for understanding the difference.

5-phase Design Thinking methodology: 1) Empathize (interviews/observation), 2) Define (problem statement), 3) Ideate (14+ ideas), 4) Prototype (low-fidelity mockup), 5) Test (validate with users). Case Study: Food delivery tracking redesign achieving -62% support messages.

6 research methods: 1) Interviews (1-on-1 qualitative), 2) Surveys (quantitative at scale), 3) Usability Testing (watch user complete task), 4) Competitor Analysis (study solutions), 5) Personas (representative profiles), 6) Journey & Flow Maps (emotional + logical paths). Case Study: Madrasti education app (+44% retention with auto-linking).

6 IA components: 1) Hierarchy (information layers), 2) Navigation (wayfinding), 3) Card Sorting (mental models), 4) Sitemap (full structure), 5) Labeling (user language), 6) Findability (search + filters + discovery). Case Study: Electronics marketplace (40→6 categories, +38% task success).
Creating effective wireframes and prototypes. Low-fidelity to high-fidelity progression. Best practices for rapid prototyping and user testing.
Core visual design principles: contrast, alignment, repetition, proximity, balance, hierarchy. Application in UI design.
Color theory for UI/UX. Creating palettes, accessibility considerations (WCAG), psychological impact, and systematic color usage.
Typography fundamentals: font selection, hierarchy, spacing, readability. Creating typographic scales and systems.
Layout principles and spacing systems. Grid systems, white space, visual rhythm, responsive layouts.
Building and maintaining design systems. Tokens, components, patterns, documentation. Examples: Material Design, Apple HIG, Ant Design.
Motion design and animation principles. Transitions, micro-interactions, easing, performance considerations.
Accessibility fundamentals and WCAG guidelines. ARIA, keyboard navigation, screen readers, color contrast, inclusive design practices.
Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics and practical application. Heuristic evaluation methodology.
Essential UX/UI design tools: Figma, Adobe XD, Sketch, prototyping tools, user testing platforms, handoff tools.
Real-world UX case studies demonstrating application of principles, research, and design processes. Before/after metrics.
Complete learning roadmap from beginner to expert UX designer. Skills progression, milestones, portfolio building.
